title: Exchange floating-point buffers with JavaScript
goal: Exchange floating-point arrays and bounded memory views with JavaScript; use direct float marshaling on .NET 11 when browser buffers need correct offsets, copy semantics and explicit lifetimes.

prerequisites: Browser-targeted project, generated imports/exports and JavaScript host; enable unsafe blocks for generated stubs.
Restore matching WebAssembly SDK/runtime package assets. This interpreted Mono route builds/publishes without wasm-tools; AOT or native relinking requires additional matching workloads.
Serve published wwwroot over HTTP(S) in a real browser; this is not a desktop .NET execution route.
platforms: Measured Mono browser-wasm in Windows Chromium; no CoreCLR-browser, AOT, other browser or OS execution claim.
renderingModes: Standalone Mono WebAssembly JavaScript host; no server circuit or Blazor component rendering required.
stabilityLimitations: Actual RC2 verification, not final-GA proof; PIN-962 and PIN-959 remain open.
constraints: Numeric arrays are copied; spans and ArraySegments use bounded MemoryViews.
Span views expire at the end of the synchronous interop call. Retained segment views pin memory; dispose in finally and do not access after disposal.
JavaScript Number/Float32 narrowing is not a precision improvement; the older double adapter has explicit copy-back costs. No throughput/allocation benchmark claim.
